newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank may lower M3 target for 1997 - DG Bank.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank may lower M3 target for 1997 - DG Bank.

text.p: The Bundesbank may lower its target corridor for M3 money supply growth, its main policy guide, to three to six percent for 1997 from the current target of four-to-seven percent growth, DG Bank said.

The target was likely to be lowered because growth in production capacity and price inflation -- two factors on which the Bundesbank bases its calculation of the target -- have slowed down, DG Bank said in a statement.

Growth in the economy's production capacity has slowed down to two percent at most, and the Bundesbank is likely to factor in an inflation rate of 1.5 percent for next year, down from two percent for 1996, DG Bank said in a statement.

DG Bank chief economist Michael Heise said there were big advantages in setting money supply targets which ran for several years but added that such a move would not be practicable now, so close to European monetary union scheduled for 1999.
The Bundesbank bases its money supply target on the development of production capacity, inflation and the velocity of money circulation.
It policy-making council meets on Thursday December 19 to set the M3 target for 1997.
